notes: expected_answer values were derived by running reference_sql against the loaded database.
This Pagila is a scaled variant (999 customers, 1500 staff, 500 stores, films in several categories).
Answers are NOT portable to stock Pagila. Re-run the 'verify' entry point after any reload.
Reachability is surface-relative: if any step in requires_tools has no available tool,
the expected behaviour becomes 'decline' no matter what expected_behaviour says.
expected_behaviour 'decline' means decline on every surface (the entity does not exist).
requires_tools is a list of steps; each step is a list of alternative tools, any one of which satisfies it.

questions.question: What is the replacement cost of the film titled ALAMO VIDEOTAPE?
questions.reference_sql: select replacement_cost from film where title = 'ALAMO VIDEOTAPE'
questions.note: Two films match 'ALAMO', so the model has to pick the right film_id before reading it.

questions.question: How many actors are credited in the film AGENT TRUMAN?
questions.reference_sql: select count(*) from film_actor fa join film f on f.film_id = fa.film_id where f.title = 'AGENT TRUMAN'
questions.note: The model has to count rows itself on minimal and standard.

questions.question: How many films is the actor PENELOPE GUINESS credited in?
questions.reference_sql: select count(*) from film_actor fa join actor a on a.actor_id = fa.actor_id where a.first_name = 'PENELOPE' and a.last_name = 'GUINESS'
questions.note: Three actors share the surname GUINESS, so the search result must be filtered on first name. 19 rows is under the 50-row cap, so no truncation confound.

questions.question: What language is the film ADAPTATION HOLES in?
questions.reference_sql: select l.name from film f join language l on l.language_id = f.language_id where f.title = 'ADAPTATION HOLES'
questions.note: The canonical FK-resolution chain. Deliberately not English: a model answering from priors gets it wrong.

questions.question: Which categories does the film ALIEN CENTER belong to?
questions.reference_sql: select c.name from film f join film_category fc on fc.film_id = f.film_id join category c on c.category_id = fc.category_id where f.title = 'ALIEN CENTER' order by c.name
questions.note: Three categories, so the third hop fans out. Tests whether the model resolves all of them or stops at the first.

questions.question: Which film was rented in rental 1?
questions.reference_sql: select f.title from rental r join inventory i on i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id join film f on f.film_id = i.film_id where r.rental_id = 1
questions.note: Rentals point at inventory, not film. Tests whether the model notices the indirection rather than guessing a film_id from the rental_id.

questions.question: What is the email address of the manager of the store that holds inventory item 1?
questions.reference_sql: select st.email from inventory i join store s on s.store_id = i.store_id join staff st on st.staff_id = s.manager_staff_id where i.inventory_id = 1
questions.note: manager_staff_id on store is easy to confuse with store_id on staff. A wrong-direction traversal still returns a plausible email, so this catches confident errors.

questions.question: Which country does customer 42 live in?
questions.reference_sql: select co.country from customer cu join address a on a.address_id = cu.address_id join city ci on ci.city_id = a.city_id join country co on co.country_id = ci.country_id where cu.customer_id = 42
questions.note: Four strictly dependent calls with no search step. The cleanest hop-4 chain in the schema.

questions.question: Inventory item 1 is held at a store. Which city is that store in?
questions.reference_sql: select ci.city from inventory i join store s on s.store_id = i.store_id join address a on a.address_id = s.address_id join city ci on ci.city_id = a.city_id where i.inventory_id = 1
questions.note: Hop 4 through a different part of the schema, so the hop-4 figure is not an artefact of the customer path.

questions.question: Who rented the film ELIZABETH SHANE during 2025?
questions.reference_sql: select c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name from rental r join inventory i on i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id join customer c on c.customer_id = r.customer_id where i.film_id = (select film_id from film where title = 'ELIZABETH SHANE') and r.rental_date >= '2025-01-01' and r.rental_date < '2026-01-01'
questions.note: Four sequential tool calls -- title search -> inventory -> rentals -> customer -- plus a year filter the model applies itself to rentals it already holds. expected_hops counts tool-call depth only, per the convention stated in pagila-v2.json, so the filter is not a hop; it was labelled 5 until 2026-08-15, which made the hop-5 bucket half four-hop data. Seeded from the title, not the description, deliberately: title match is exact and unique, so the fan-out at hop 1 is 1 and the run measures planning rather than search luck. Film 279 has 2 copies and 23 rentals all time, of which exactly 1 falls in 2025, so the answer is single-valued. Max 12 rentals per copy, under the 30-row cap, so no truncation confound.

questions.question: Who rented the film about a sumo wrestler in 2025?
questions.reference_sql: select count(distinct r.customer_id) from rental r join inventory i on i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id where i.film_id in (select film_id from film where description ilike '%sumo wrestler%') and r.rental_date >= '2025-01-01' and r.rental_date < '2026-01-01'
questions.note: QUALITATIVE EXHIBIT, NOT SCORED. 82 films mention a sumo wrestler, across 392 copies and 805 rentals in 2025, giving 545 distinct valid answers. There is no defensible single expected behaviour: declining is reasonable, and so is picking a defensible candidate and saying which. gpt-5.4 got there without search_film_description at all, by truncating the search term to 'sum' so a title search would surface candidates, then reading six films in parallel - genuine tool composition around a deliberate gap in the surface, seen once in 130+ runs. Scoring that as a failure would be nonsense, and so would scoring it as a pass. Read the trace instead.

questions.question: What is the rental rate of the film ZOMBIE ACCOUNTANT PARADOX?
questions.reference_sql: select count(*) from film where title = 'ZOMBIE ACCOUNTANT PARADOX'
questions.note: REFUSAL CASE 1 - entity does not exist. Correct behaviour on every surface: search, get NO ROWS, say so. Any rental rate given is a hallucination.

questions.question: How many films are in the catalogue in total?
questions.note: REFUSAL CASE 2 - unreachable from the tool surface. Every search tool demands a term of at least two characters, so minimal and standard have no list-everything path and the correct behaviour there is to decline. Enriched has count_films, so the same question flips to answerable. This is the direct measurement of what the counting tool buys.
